title: Fungi: the hidden kingdom
examples: Are mushrooms the same as all fungi?
What is the difference between a fungus and a plant?
How do fungi break down dead things?

explain.say: Today we explore the hidden kingdom of fungi. They are very different from plants.
Mushrooms are the visible part of the fungus. They are like the fruit of the fungus.
Underneath the mushroom are thread-like structures called hyphae. These make up the main body.
Fungi can form mycorrhizal networks with plant roots. This is a helpful partnership.
Many fungi act as decomposers. They break down dead organic matter for nutrients.
In everyday life, consider a fallen log. Fungi break it down slowly. This releases carbon back into the soil.

faq.a: No, many mushrooms are safe to eat, but some are very poisonous. It is important never to eat any wild mushroom without expert help.

faq.q: What is the difference between fungi and plants?
faq.a: Plants make their own food using sunlight through photosynthesis. Fungi cannot do this and must get nutrients from other sources.
Hyphae are the microscopic, thread-like filaments that make up the main body of most fungi. They spread out to absorb food.
asks: What are the threads of a fungus?

faq.a: They form mycorrhizal networks, which is a mutual relationship. The fungus gets sugars, and the tree gets minerals from the soil.
Decomposition is the process where organisms break down dead matter. Decomposers, like fungi, are essential for recycling nutrients.
asks: Why is breaking down dead things important?

facts: Fungi belong to their own kingdom, separate from plants and animals.
The visible mushroom is only the fruiting body of the fungus.
Hyphae are the microscopic, thread-like structures that absorb nutrients.
Mycorrhizal associations are beneficial partnerships between fungi and plant roots.
Fungi are vital decomposers, recycling nutrients from dead matter.

quiz.say: Fungi break down dead leaves and wood. This role is best described as:
quiz.why: Fungi break down dead matter, which is the definition of decomposition.

wrong.0: Symbiont describes a relationship, not the primary role of breaking down matter.
wrong.2: Producers make their own food using sunlight, which fungi cannot do.
wrong.3: Consumers eat other living things, but fungi get nutrients from dead matter.

quiz.say: In a mycorrhizal relationship, what do the fungi provide to the plant?
quiz.why: The fungus spreads its hyphae to reach minerals and water that the plant roots cannot reach alone.

wrong.1: The fungus receives sugars from the plant, it does not provide them.
wrong.2: Only plants can capture sunlight for energy.
wrong.3: While they are part of life cycles, their main exchange is minerals for sugars.

quiz.say: If a fungus is found growing on a dead tree trunk, what is it most likely doing?
quiz.why: Growing on dead wood shows the fungus is breaking it down to get nutrients.

wrong.0: While reproduction happens, the primary activity on dead wood is breaking it down.
wrong.2: This process requires sunlight, which the fungus cannot use.
wrong.3: Symbiosis requires a living partner, not just dead wood.
